CNBC, "U.S. and Iran pause fighting to give peace talks 'space.' Here's where negotiations stand", 27 July 2026:
- A temporary pause to the U.S.-Iran conflict appeared to hold on Monday, even as Tehran denied media reports that it had agreed to a 10-day ceasefire.
- US and Iran appear to have stopped strikes for a third day in a row.
- A combat hiatus began Friday, following nearly two weeks of U.S. strikes against Iran in retaliation for attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
- Iran has not launched drone or missile strikes on Saudi Arabia or other Persian Gulf states since U.S. forces paused their attacks on Saturday.
- Regional mediators have presented Washington and Tehran with a proposal for a 10-day ceasefire, which could put last month's memorandum of understanding back on track.
- Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei on Monday said Iran "currently have no negotiations with the United States," reiterating that official talks are solely with Oman regarding the future of the Strait of Hormuz.
- Saudi air defenses intercepted several drones launched from Iraq on Monday targeting petroleum facilities. Major General Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson for Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Defense: the "terrorist attempts were launched from Iraqi territory and carried out by terrorist militias affiliated with Iran."
- Brent crude fell below $90 (to around $89-$90) as the pause held; Brent for September fell roughly 6.7-7.4% intraday.
